about: Baby Insanity Wolf is a photo of a fluffy grey wolf pup sitting in a meadow of pink wildflowers, head tipped back mid-howl. It is the miniature version of Insanity Wolf, the advice animal that shouted extreme, violent "rules". The pup's rebellions are tiny and mostly harmless: eating dessert first, wearing socks with sandals, using the pen that was on the teacher's desk. The joke is the gap between the fierce howl and how small the act of defiance actually is.
origin: It grew out of the Insanity Wolf advice animal as a cuter, toned-down offshoot that applies the same rebellious attitude to minor misbehavior.
usage:
The top box is the small rule-breaking act, written in the clipped advice-animal voice. The bottom box makes it even more defiant or adds the detail that tips it into mild chaos. Example: "gets iced coffee" / "in the winter".

The tinier the rebellion, the better it fits. Leaving one second on the microwave, opening a new milk before finishing the old one, wearing a hoodie in summer, or replying "k" are perfect. Avoid anything genuinely harmful; the joke is that this wolf is all bark.
ideas: on a library book's sticky note
